### A Name Like No Other
Author: Alistair Begg
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/truth-for-life/truth-for-life-august-29-2024.html
Passage: Psalm 148:13
Points:
- God’s name reveals His true nature, character, and eternal attributes.
- By identifying Himself as "I am," the Lord separates Himself from all false gods.
- Humanly crafted idols demand devotion but are powerless to save or deliver.
- Because God is uncreated, self-existent, and completely sovereign, His name alone is exalted.
- Worshiping God properly requires tearing down idols that compete for our ultimate affection.

### What Do You Believe about Creation?
Author: Adrian Rogers
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/loveworthfinding/love-worth-finding-august-31-2019.html
Passage: Psalm 148:5
Points:
- God spoke the physical cosmos into being by the sovereign power of His command.
- Humanity is not the product of random chance but the purposeful design of the Creator.
- While the universe was brought forth by spoken words, redemption required the cross of Jesus Christ.
- Through Christ's sacrifice, believers are made into an entirely new creation.

### The Bible Is Always Ahead of Science
Author: Rick Warren
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/daily-hope-with-rick-warren/daily-hope-with-rick-warren-june-8-2023.html
Passage: Psalm 148:4-6
Points:
- True science and God's Word agree because the same God authored both.
- While not a technical textbook, Scripture accurately anticipates principles governing the physical universe.
- The laws of nature operate reliably because God established them by decree.
- The enduring order of heaven and earth points back to an unchanging Creator.

### Cricket Places
Author: Chuck Swindoll
Site: Insight for Living
URL: https://insight.org/resources/daily-devotional/individual/cricket-places1
Passage: Psalm 148
Points:
- God's varied creation constantly declares His greatness in ways people often overlook.
- Human beings easily become trapped in predictable routines and dull familiarity.
- Pausing to experience God's wilderness, waters, and creatures revives a sense of wonder.
- Stepping away into creation provides space to reflect on the Maker and break spiritual monotony.
